exposure: mode of birth (vaginal delivery vs cesarean section)
outcome: health burden (maternal and neonatal lives and health)
cohort: The participants were a sample of women consulting primary healthcare centers after delivery for the vaccination of their children.
finding: The prevalence of cesarean delivery among the study participants exceeded 50%, imposing a significant financial and health burden on the community, with most operations performed in private hospitals.
mod_finding: Cesarean sections impose a significant financial and health burden in comparison with normal vaginal delivery.
cross-section timing: after delivery for vaccination of their children
